locator.text: Display 81.1, p. 81, in the proof of Lemma 7.4

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. No declaration forms the quotient r = z₋/z₊ or asserts that it is differentiable with this derivative; I searched the sources and the index and found no Riccati/quotient ODE anywhere (the only occurrences of this polynomial in NavierStokes/ are GrowingMode.lean lines 76 and 92). The Lean takes another route, which its own module docstring states: "The invariant region is proved using a quadratic boundary function, without dividing by the growing coordinate or assuming its positivity along the solution." In place of r it uses barrier t = (z t 1)² - r²(z t 0)² with r a *constant* half-width (a name collision with the paper's ratio function), and shows barrier ≤ 0 by a boundary-derivative argument. The two formulas are linked exactly: writing u = z₋/z₊, d/dt[z₋² - r²z₊²] = 2 z₊² u u' + 2 z₊ z₊'(u² - r²), so at u = ±r the barrier derivative is ±2 r z₊² times the display's right-hand side — and that right-hand side appears verbatim as the subject of upper_edge_factor_negative. The initial condition r(0) = 0 is stated, in the modal coordinates, by primary_initial (z₋(a) = 0 with z₊(a) = P(a) > 0). Only the paper's intermediate formula, not its conclusion, is missing: the cone bound it is used to prove is established (positive_invariant_cone, scaled_positive_invariant_cone).
